**Indore district** (Hindi pronunciation:[[ɪn̪d̪ɔːɾ]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:IPA/Hindi_and_Urdu "Help:IPA/Hindi and Urdu")) is a [district](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_districts_of_Madhya_Pradesh "List of districts of Madhya Pradesh") of [Madhya Pradesh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Madhya_Pradesh "Madhya Pradesh") state in central [India](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/India "India"). It is believed that the city is named after its Indreshwar Mahadev Temple, where Indra is the presiding deity as Indra+Oor. The Gupta inscriptions name Indore as "Indrapura". It is also called the administrative capital. This district forms part of the [Indore Division](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore_Division "Indore Division").
As of 2011, it was the most populous of the [50 districts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Districts_of_Madhya_Pradesh "Districts of Madhya Pradesh") in Madhya Pradesh.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore_district#cite_note-districtcensus-4)
Indore is the administrative center of district, and largest city of Madhya Pradesh.

The Indore District has an area of 3,898 km 2[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore_district#cite_note-5) and borders the districts of [Ujjain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ujjain_District "Ujjain District") to the north, [Dewas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dewas_District "Dewas District") to the east, [Khargone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Khargone_District "Khargone District") to the south, and [Dhar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dhar_District "Dhar District") to the west.
The two main rivers of the Indore district are the [Chambal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chambal_River "Chambal River"), in the west, (originating in the Vindhya range south of Mhow) and the [Kshipra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kshipra_River "Kshipra River"), a tributary of the [Chambal river](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chambal_River "Chambal River"), in the east. Other small rivers include the [Gambhir](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gambhir_River_(Madhya_Pradesh) "Gambhir River (Madhya Pradesh)") and the Kanh, both tributaries of the [Kshipra river](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kshipra_River "Kshipra River").
Indore is the administrative centre and main city in the district. [Dr. Ambedkar Nagar (Mhow)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mhow "Mhow") is an important [cantonment](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cantonment "Cantonment") town in the Indore District that contains three of the [Indian Army](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_Army "Indian Army")'s premier training institutes, as well as the [Border Security Force](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Border_Security_Force "Border Security Force")'s Central School of Weapons and Tactics (CSWT). Other towns in Indore include [Depalpur](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Depalpur_(India) "Depalpur (India)"), Sanwer and Hatod.

The [municipalities](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Municipal_council_(India) "Municipal council (India)") of Indore district are listed as follows:

*   [Sanwer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sanwer "Sanwer")
There are also four [blocks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Block_(district_subdivision) "Block (district subdivision)")[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore_district#cite_note-7) in the district, with 51 police stations.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore_district#cite_note-8)
*   [Indore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore "Indore")  
*   [Dr. Ambedkar Nagar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dr._Ambedkar_Nagar "Dr. Ambedkar Nagar")  
*   [Sanwer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sanwer "Sanwer")  
*   [Depalpur](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Depalpur,_India "Depalpur, India")
There are a total of 335 Panchayats and 649 villages in the four blocks.

On June 4, 2024, Shri.Shankar Lalwani of Bharatiya Janata Party has been re-elected as the Member of Parliament from Indore constituency, with the highest national margin.[8]
In May 2019, Shankar Lalwani of [Bharatiya Janata Party](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bharatiya_Janata_Party "Bharatiya Janata Party") had been elected as the [Member of Parliament](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Member_of_parliament,_Lok_Sabha "Member of parliament, Lok Sabha") from Indore constituency.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore_district#cite_note-9)
The previous member of the Lok Sabha from the Indore constituency was [Sumitra Mahajan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sumitra_Mahajan "Sumitra Mahajan") of the [Bharatiya Janata Party](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bharatiya_Janata_Party "Bharatiya Janata Party") (BJP). She was a Member of Parliament from 1989 to May 2019.

Since parliamentary and legislative assembly constituency boundaries were redrawn in 2008, there have been nine [Vidhan Sabha](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Madhya_Pradesh_Vidhan_Sabha "Madhya Pradesh Vidhan Sabha") constituencies in this district: Depalpur, Indore-1, Indore-2, Indore-3, Indore-4, Indore-5, [Dr. Ambedkar Nagar-Mhow](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dr._Ambedkar_Nagar-Mhow_(Vidhan_Sabha_constituency) "Dr. Ambedkar Nagar-Mhow (Vidhan Sabha constituency)"), Rau and Sanwer.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore_district#cite_note-10)[Dr. Ambedkar Nagar-Mhow](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dr._Ambedkar_Nagar-Mhow_(Vidhan_Sabha_constituency) "Dr. Ambedkar Nagar-Mhow (Vidhan Sabha constituency)") is part of the [Dhar Lok Sabha constituency](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dhar_(Lok_Sabha_constituency) "Dhar (Lok Sabha constituency)") and the others are part of the [Indore Lok Sabha constituency](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore_(Lok_Sabha_constituency) "Indore (Lok Sabha constituency)").
The electricity in Indore district is distributed by Madhya Pradesh Paschim Kshetra Vidyut Vitaran Company Limited.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore_district#cite_note-11)

In May 2019, Shankar Lalwani of [Bharatiya Janata Party](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bharatiya_Janata_Party "Bharatiya Janata Party") had been elected as the [Member of Parliament](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Member_of_parliament,_Lok_Sabha "Member of parliament, Lok Sabha") from Indore constituency.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore_district#cite_note-9)
The previous member of the Lok Sabha from the Indore constituency was [Sumitra Mahajan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sumitra_Mahajan "Sumitra Mahajan") of the [Bharatiya Janata Party](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bharatiya_Janata_Party "Bharatiya Janata Party") (BJP). She was a Member of Parliament from 1989 to May 2019.
texts.9:
Since parliamentary and legislative assembly constituency boundaries were redrawn in 2008, there have been nine [Vidhan Sabha](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Madhya_Pradesh_Vidhan_Sabha "Madhya Pradesh Vidhan Sabha") constituencies in this district: Depalpur, Indore-1, Indore-2, Indore-3, Indore-4, Indore-5, [Dr. Ambedkar Nagar-Mhow](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dr._Ambedkar_Nagar-Mhow_(Vidhan_Sabha_constituency) "Dr. Ambedkar Nagar-Mhow (Vidhan Sabha constituency)"), Rau and Sanwer.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore_district#cite_note-10)[Dr. Ambedkar Nagar-Mhow](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dr._Ambedkar_Nagar-Mhow_(Vidhan_Sabha_constituency) "Dr. Ambedkar Nagar-Mhow (Vidhan Sabha constituency)") is part of the [Dhar Lok Sabha constituency](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dhar_(Lok_Sabha_constituency) "Dhar (Lok Sabha constituency)") and the others are part of the [Indore Lok Sabha constituency](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore_(Lok_Sabha_constituency) "Indore (Lok Sabha constituency)").
The electricity in Indore district is distributed by Madhya Pradesh Paschim Kshetra Vidyut Vitaran Company Limited.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore_district#cite_note-11)

**Indore district** (Hindi pronunciation:[[ɪn̪d̪ɔːɾ]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:IPA/Hindi_and_Urdu "Help:IPA/Hindi and Urdu")) is a [district](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_districts_of_Madhya_Pradesh "List of districts of Madhya Pradesh") of [Madhya Pradesh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Madhya_Pradesh "Madhya Pradesh") state in central [India](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/India "India"). It is believed that the city is named after its Indreshwar Mahadev Temple, where Indra is the presiding deity as Indra+Oor. The Gupta inscriptions name Indore as "Indrapura". It is also called the administrative capital. This district forms part of the [Indore Division](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore_Division "Indore Division").
As of 2011, it was the most populous of the [50 districts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Districts_of_Madhya_Pradesh "Districts of Madhya Pradesh") in Madhya Pradesh.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore_district#cite_note-districtcensus-4)
Indore is the administrative center of district, and largest city of Madhya Pradesh.

The Indore District has an area of 3,898 km 2[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore_district#cite_note-5) and borders the districts of [Ujjain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ujjain_District "Ujjain District") to the north, [Dewas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dewas_District "Dewas District") to the east, [Khargone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Khargone_District "Khargone District") to the south, and [Dhar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dhar_District "Dhar District") to the west.
The two main rivers of the Indore district are the [Chambal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chambal_River "Chambal River"), in the west, (originating in the Vindhya range south of Mhow) and the [Kshipra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kshipra_River "Kshipra River"), a tributary of the [Chambal river](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chambal_River "Chambal River"), in the east. Other small rivers include the [Gambhir](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gambhir_River_(Madhya_Pradesh) "Gambhir River (Madhya Pradesh)") and the Kanh, both tributaries of the [Kshipra river](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kshipra_River "Kshipra River").
Indore is the administrative centre and main city in the district. [Dr. Ambedkar Nagar (Mhow)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mhow "Mhow") is an important [cantonment](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cantonment "Cantonment") town in the Indore District that contains three of the [Indian Army](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_Army "Indian Army")'s premier training institutes, as well as the [Border Security Force](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Border_Security_Force "Border Security Force")'s Central School of Weapons and Tactics (CSWT). Other towns in Indore include [Depalpur](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Depalpur_(India) "Depalpur (India)"), Sanwer and Hatod.

The [municipalities](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Municipal_council_(India) "Municipal council (India)") of Indore district are listed as follows:

There are also four [blocks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Block_(district_subdivision) "Block (district subdivision)")[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore_district#cite_note-7) in the district, with 51 police stations.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore_district#cite_note-8)
*   [Indore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore "Indore")  
*   [Dr. Ambedkar Nagar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dr._Ambedkar_Nagar "Dr. Ambedkar Nagar")  
*   [Sanwer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sanwer "Sanwer")  
*   [Depalpur](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Depalpur,_India "Depalpur, India")
There are a total of 335 Panchayats and 649 villages in the four blocks.

On June 4, 2024, Shri.Shankar Lalwani of Bharatiya Janata Party has been re-elected as the Member of Parliament from Indore constituency, with the highest national margin.[8]
In May 2019, Shankar Lalwani of [Bharatiya Janata Party](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bharatiya_Janata_Party "Bharatiya Janata Party") had been elected as the [Member of Parliament](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Member_of_parliament,_Lok_Sabha "Member of parliament, Lok Sabha") from Indore constituency.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore_district#cite_note-9)
The previous member of the Lok Sabha from the Indore constituency was [Sumitra Mahajan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sumitra_Mahajan "Sumitra Mahajan") of the [Bharatiya Janata Party](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bharatiya_Janata_Party "Bharatiya Janata Party") (BJP). She was a Member of Parliament from 1989 to May 2019.

Since parliamentary and legislative assembly constituency boundaries were redrawn in 2008, there have been nine [Vidhan Sabha](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Madhya_Pradesh_Vidhan_Sabha "Madhya Pradesh Vidhan Sabha") constituencies in this district: Depalpur, Indore-1, Indore-2, Indore-3, Indore-4, Indore-5, [Dr. Ambedkar Nagar-Mhow](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dr._Ambedkar_Nagar-Mhow_(Vidhan_Sabha_constituency) "Dr. Ambedkar Nagar-Mhow (Vidhan Sabha constituency)"), Rau and Sanwer.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore_district#cite_note-10)[Dr. Ambedkar Nagar-Mhow](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dr._Ambedkar_Nagar-Mhow_(Vidhan_Sabha_constituency) "Dr. Ambedkar Nagar-Mhow (Vidhan Sabha constituency)") is part of the [Dhar Lok Sabha constituency](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dhar_(Lok_Sabha_constituency) "Dhar (Lok Sabha constituency)") and the others are part of the [Indore Lok Sabha constituency](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore_(Lok_Sabha_constituency) "Indore (Lok Sabha constituency)").
The electricity in Indore district is distributed by Madhya Pradesh Paschim Kshetra Vidyut Vitaran Company Limited.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore_district#cite_note-11)

According to the [2011 census](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_census_of_India "2011 census of India"),

the Indore District has a [population](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Demographics_of_India "Demographics of India") of 3,276,697,[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore_district#cite_note-districtcensus-4) which roughly equals the nation of [Mauritania](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mauritania "Mauritania")[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore_district#cite_note-cia-14) or the US state of [Iowa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iowa "Iowa").[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore_district#cite_note-15) This makes it the 105th most populous in India (out of a total of [640](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Districts_of_India "Districts of India")) districts.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore_district#cite_note-districtcensus-4) The district has a population density of 841 inhabitants per square kilometre (2,180/sq mi).[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore_district#cite_note-districtcensus-4) Its [population growth rate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Family_planning_in_India "Family planning in India") over the decade 2001-2011 was 32.88%.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore_district#cite_note-districtcensus-4) Indore has a [sex ratio](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sex_ratio "Sex ratio") of 928 [females](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Women_in_India "Women in India") for every 1,000 males,[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore_district#cite_note-districtcensus-4) and a [literacy rate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Literacy_in_India "Literacy in India") of 80.87% (male 87.25% and female 74.02%).

74.09% of the population lives in urban areas. Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes make up 16.64% and 6.64% of the population respectively.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore_district#cite_note-districtcensus-4)
At the time of the [2011 Census of India](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Census_of_India "2011 Census of India"), 71.39% of the population in the district spoke [Hindi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hindi "Hindi"), 15.05% [Malvi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malvi_language "Malvi language"), 3.54% [Marathi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marathi_language "Marathi language"), 2.81% [Urdu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urdu "Urdu"), 1.74% [Sindhi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sindhi_language "Sindhi language"), 1.39% [Nimadi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nimadi_language "Nimadi language"), 0.98% [Gujarati](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gujarati_language "Gujarati language"), 0.81% [Punjabi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Punjabi_language "Punjabi language") and 0.49% [Bhili](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bhili_language "Bhili language") as their first language.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore_district#cite_note-language-16)

Indore district has the variety of tourist spots, historical spots and natural spots for the purpose of tourism. [Indore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore "Indore") city has palaces of the erstwhile [Holkar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/House_of_Holkar "House of Holkar") rulers.

*   Dr. Babasaheb Ambedkar, Birth Place

*   [Rajwada](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rajwada "Rajwada") - Also known as the Holkar Palace, Rajwada is a seven-story palace in the heart of Indore. It was built in the 18th century by the Holkar dynasty and is an example of the fusion of Maratha, Mughal, and French architecture.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore_district#cite_note-17)  
*   [Lal Bagh Palace](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lalbagh_Palace "Lalbagh Palace") - Lal Bagh Palace is another palace built by the Holkar dynasty, located on the outskirts of Indore. It was built in the 19th century and is now a museum that houses the Holkar family's belongings, including paintings, weapons, and furniture.  
*   Annapurna Temple[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore_district#cite_note-18) - The Annapurna Temple is dedicated to the Hindu goddess of food and nourishment, Annapurna. It is located in the heart of Indore and is known for its stunning architecture and intricate carvings.  
*   [Khajrana Ganesh Temple](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Khajrana_Ganesh_Temple "Khajrana Ganesh Temple") - The Khajrana Ganesh Temple is one of the most popular temples in Indore, dedicated to Lord Ganesha, the elephant-headed god of wisdom and prosperity. It is believed to be one of the oldest temples in the city and is visited by thousands of devotees every day.  
*   [Kanch Mandir](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kanch_Mandir "Kanch Mandir") - Kanch Mandir, also known as the Glass Temple, is a Jain temple in Indore that is entirely made of glass. It was built in the early 20th century and is known for its intricate glasswork and stunning architecture.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore_district#cite_note-19)

*   [Jam Gate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jam_Gate "Jam Gate") – Jam Gate is a historic gateway located near Mhow on the Indore–Mandleshwar Road. It is known for its historical significance and panoramic views.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore_district#cite_note-20)[![Image 8](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/7f/Jam_Gate%2C_Indore_district%2CMonuments_and_memorials_in_Madhya_Pradesh%2C_Gates_in_India.jpg/250px-Jam_Gate%2C_Indore_district%2CMonuments_and_memorials_in_Madhya_Pradesh%2C_Gates_in_India.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Jam_Gate,_Indore_district,Monuments_and_memorials_in_Madhya_Pradesh,_Gates_in_India.jpg)
Jam Gate near Mhow, Indore district, Madhya Pradesh

*   [Patalpani Waterfall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Patalpani_waterfall "Patalpani waterfall") - Patalpani Waterfall is a stunning waterfall located on the outskirts of Indore. It is one of the highest waterfalls in Madhya Pradesh, with water cascading down from a height of 300 feet. The surrounding area is covered with lush green forests, making it a popular spot for picnics and treks.  
*   [Tincha Falls](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tincha_waterfall "Tincha waterfall") - Tincha Falls is another waterfall located near Indore, surrounded by dense forests and hills. It is a picturesque spot for nature lovers and adventure enthusiasts, offering activities like trekking, rappelling, and rock climbing.  
*   [Ralamandal Wildlife Sanctuary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ralamandal_Wildlife_Sanctuary "Ralamandal Wildlife Sanctuary") - Ralamandal Wildlife Sanctuary is a lush green forest located in the outskirts of Indore. It is home to several species of [flora and fauna](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Organism "Organism"), including the Indian leopard, [sambar deer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sambar_deer "Sambar deer"), [wild boar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wild_boar "Wild boar"), and Indian giant squirrel. Visitors can enjoy trekking, bird watching, and nature walks in the sanctuary.  
*   [Mandu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mandu,_Madhya_Pradesh "Mandu, Madhya Pradesh") - Mandu is a historical town located in the Dhar district of Madhya Pradesh. It is surrounded by forests and hills and is home to several ancient ruins, including the Jahaz Mahal, [Hindola Mahal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hindola_Mahal "Hindola Mahal"), and the Baz Bahadur Palace.  
*   Choral Dam - Choral Dam is located near Indore. The surrounding area is covered with lush green forests and hills, making it an ideal spot for picnics and water sports like [boating](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boating "Boating") and [fishing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fishing "Fishing").[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

**Indore district** (Hindi pronunciation:[[ɪn̪d̪ɔːɾ]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:IPA/Hindi_and_Urdu "Help:IPA/Hindi and Urdu")) is a [district](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_districts_of_Madhya_Pradesh "List of districts of Madhya Pradesh") of [Madhya Pradesh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Madhya_Pradesh "Madhya Pradesh") state in central [India](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/India "India"). It is believed that the city is named after its Indreshwar Mahadev Temple, where Indra is the presiding deity as Indra+Oor. The Gupta inscriptions name Indore as "Indrapura". It is also called the administrative capital. This district forms part of the [Indore Division](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore_Division "Indore Division").
As of 2011, it was the most populous of the [50 districts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Districts_of_Madhya_Pradesh "Districts of Madhya Pradesh") in Madhya Pradesh.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore_district#cite_note-districtcensus-4)
Indore is the administrative center of district, and largest city of Madhya Pradesh.
texts.5:
The Indore District has an area of 3,898 km 2[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore_district#cite_note-5) and borders the districts of [Ujjain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ujjain_District "Ujjain District") to the north, [Dewas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dewas_District "Dewas District") to the east, [Khargone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Khargone_District "Khargone District") to the south, and [Dhar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dhar_District "Dhar District") to the west.
The two main rivers of the Indore district are the [Chambal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chambal_River "Chambal River"), in the west, (originating in the Vindhya range south of Mhow) and the [Kshipra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kshipra_River "Kshipra River"), a tributary of the [Chambal river](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chambal_River "Chambal River"), in the east. Other small rivers include the [Gambhir](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gambhir_River_(Madhya_Pradesh) "Gambhir River (Madhya Pradesh)") and the Kanh, both tributaries of the [Kshipra river](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kshipra_River "Kshipra River").
Indore is the administrative centre and main city in the district. [Dr. Ambedkar Nagar (Mhow)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mhow "Mhow") is an important [cantonment](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cantonment "Cantonment") town in the Indore District that contains three of the [Indian Army](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_Army "Indian Army")'s premier training institutes, as well as the [Border Security Force](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Border_Security_Force "Border Security Force")'s Central School of Weapons and Tactics (CSWT). Other towns in Indore include [Depalpur](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Depalpur_(India) "Depalpur (India)"), Sanwer and Hatod.

texts.8:
On June 4, 2024, Shri.Shankar Lalwani of Bharatiya Janata Party has been re-elected as the Member of Parliament from Indore constituency, with the highest national margin.[8]
In May 2019, Shankar Lalwani of [Bharatiya Janata Party](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bharatiya_Janata_Party "Bharatiya Janata Party") had been elected as the [Member of Parliament](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Member_of_parliament,_Lok_Sabha "Member of parliament, Lok Sabha") from Indore constituency.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore_district#cite_note-9)
The previous member of the Lok Sabha from the Indore constituency was [Sumitra Mahajan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sumitra_Mahajan "Sumitra Mahajan") of the [Bharatiya Janata Party](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bharatiya_Janata_Party "Bharatiya Janata Party") (BJP). She was a Member of Parliament from 1989 to May 2019.
texts.9:
Since parliamentary and legislative assembly constituency boundaries were redrawn in 2008, there have been nine [Vidhan Sabha](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Madhya_Pradesh_Vidhan_Sabha "Madhya Pradesh Vidhan Sabha") constituencies in this district: Depalpur, Indore-1, Indore-2, Indore-3, Indore-4, Indore-5, [Dr. Ambedkar Nagar-Mhow](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dr._Ambedkar_Nagar-Mhow_(Vidhan_Sabha_constituency) "Dr. Ambedkar Nagar-Mhow (Vidhan Sabha constituency)"), Rau and Sanwer.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore_district#cite_note-10)[Dr. Ambedkar Nagar-Mhow](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dr._Ambedkar_Nagar-Mhow_(Vidhan_Sabha_constituency) "Dr. Ambedkar Nagar-Mhow (Vidhan Sabha constituency)") is part of the [Dhar Lok Sabha constituency](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dhar_(Lok_Sabha_constituency) "Dhar (Lok Sabha constituency)") and the others are part of the [Indore Lok Sabha constituency](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore_(Lok_Sabha_constituency) "Indore (Lok Sabha constituency)").
The electricity in Indore district is distributed by Madhya Pradesh Paschim Kshetra Vidyut Vitaran Company Limited.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore_district#cite_note-11)

texts.12: the Indore District has a [population](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Demographics_of_India "Demographics of India") of 3,276,697,[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore_district#cite_note-districtcensus-4) which roughly equals the nation of [Mauritania](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mauritania "Mauritania")[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore_district#cite_note-cia-14) or the US state of [Iowa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iowa "Iowa").[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore_district#cite_note-15) This makes it the 105th most populous in India (out of a total of [640](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Districts_of_India "Districts of India")) districts.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore_district#cite_note-districtcensus-4) The district has a population density of 841 inhabitants per square kilometre (2,180/sq mi).[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore_district#cite_note-districtcensus-4) Its [population growth rate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Family_planning_in_India "Family planning in India") over the decade 2001-2011 was 32.88%.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore_district#cite_note-districtcensus-4) Indore has a [sex ratio](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sex_ratio "Sex ratio") of 928 [females](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Women_in_India "Women in India") for every 1,000 males,[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore_district#cite_note-districtcensus-4) and a [literacy rate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Literacy_in_India "Literacy in India") of 80.87% (male 87.25% and female 74.02%).
texts.13:
74.09% of the population lives in urban areas. Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes make up 16.64% and 6.64% of the population respectively.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore_district#cite_note-districtcensus-4)
At the time of the [2011 Census of India](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Census_of_India "2011 Census of India"), 71.39% of the population in the district spoke [Hindi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hindi "Hindi"), 15.05% [Malvi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malvi_language "Malvi language"), 3.54% [Marathi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marathi_language "Marathi language"), 2.81% [Urdu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urdu "Urdu"), 1.74% [Sindhi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sindhi_language "Sindhi language"), 1.39% [Nimadi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nimadi_language "Nimadi language"), 0.98% [Gujarati](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gujarati_language "Gujarati language"), 0.81% [Punjabi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Punjabi_language "Punjabi language") and 0.49% [Bhili](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bhili_language "Bhili language") as their first language.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore_district#cite_note-language-16)

It was built in the 18th century by the Holkar dynasty and is an example of the fusion of Maratha, Mughal, and French architecture.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore_district#cite_note-17)  
*   [Lal Bagh Palace](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lalbagh_Palace "Lalbagh Palace") - Lal Bagh Palace is another palace built by the Holkar dynasty, located on the outskirts of Indore. It was built in the 19th century and is now a museum that houses the Holkar family's belongings, including paintings, weapons, and furniture.  
*   Annapurna Temple[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore_district#cite_note-18) - The Annapurna Temple is dedicated to the Hindu goddess of food and nourishment, Annapurna. It is located in the heart of Indore and is known for its stunning architecture and intricate carvings.  
*   [Khajrana Ganesh Temple](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Khajrana_Ganesh_Temple "Khajrana Ganesh Temple") - The Khajrana Ganesh Temple is one of the most popular temples in Indore, dedicated to Lord Ganesha, the elephant-headed god of wisdom and prosperity. It is believed to be one of the oldest temples in the city and is visited by thousands of devotees every day.  
*   [Kanch Mandir](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kanch_Mandir "Kanch Mandir") - Kanch Mandir, also known as the Glass Temple, is a Jain temple in Indore that is entirely made of glass. It was built in the early 20th century and is known for its intricate glasswork and stunning architecture.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore_district#cite_note-19)
texts.17:

texts.18:

It is one of the highest waterfalls in Madhya Pradesh, with water cascading down from a height of 300 feet. The surrounding area is covered with lush green forests, making it a popular spot for picnics and treks.

It is a picturesque spot for nature lovers and adventure enthusiasts, offering activities like trekking, rappelling, and rock climbing.  
*   [Ralamandal Wildlife Sanctuary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ralamandal_Wildlife_Sanctuary "Ralamandal Wildlife Sanctuary") - Ralamandal Wildlife Sanctuary is a lush green forest located in the outskirts of Indore. It is home to several species of [flora and fauna](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Organism "Organism"), including the Indian leopard, [sambar deer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sambar_deer "Sambar deer"), [wild boar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wild_boar "Wild boar"), and Indian giant squirrel. Visitors can enjoy trekking, bird watching, and nature walks in the sanctuary.  
*   [Mandu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mandu,_Madhya_Pradesh "Mandu, Madhya Pradesh") - Mandu is a historical town located in the Dhar district of Madhya Pradesh. It is surrounded by forests and hills and is home to several ancient ruins, including the Jahaz Mahal, [Hindola Mahal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hindola_Mahal "Hindola Mahal"), and the Baz Bahadur Palace.  
*   Choral Dam - Choral Dam is located near Indore. The surrounding area is covered with lush green forests and hills, making it an ideal spot for picnics and water sports like [boating](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boating "Boating") and [fishing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fishing "Fishing").[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

# Ujjain Lok Sabha constituency
| Elected year | [2024](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_general_election,_2024 "Indian general election, 2024") |
**Ujjain** is one of the 29 [Lok Sabha](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lok_Sabha "Lok Sabha") constituencies in the [Indian state](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/States_and_union_territories_of_India "States and union territories of India") of [Madhya Pradesh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Madhya_Pradesh "Madhya Pradesh"). It covers the entire [Ujjain district](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ujjain_district "Ujjain district") and part of [Ratlam district](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ratlam_district "Ratlam district"). This constituency came into existence in 1951 as one of the [9th Lok Sabha](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/9th_Lok_Sabha "9th Lok Sabha") constituencies in the erstwhile [Madhya Bharat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Madhya_Bharat "Madhya Bharat") state. It has been reserved for candidates belonging to [scheduled castes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dalit "Dalit") since 1966.

# Ujjain Lok Sabha Election results 2024
Ujjain, a Lok Sabha constituency in Madhya Pradesh, was formed in 1951 and is one of 29 constituencies in the state. It includes Ujjain and part of Ratlam district. Reserved for scheduled caste candidates since 1966, the 2019 election saw Anil Firojiya of BJP emerge victorious with a significant margin of 3,65,637 votes over Babulal Malviya of INC. Firojiya secured 7,91,663 votes, retaining his position as the current MP. The constituency comprises Mahidpur, Ujjain Dakshin, Nagada-khachrod, Tarana (sc), Alot (sc), Badnagar, Ujjain Uttar, and Ghatiya (sc) assembly constituencies. Notable for a 75.33% voter turnout in 2019, 10 candidates contested. Ujjain Lok Sabha constituency remains a significant political area in Madhya Pradesh.

# Ujjain Lok Sabha constituency
| Elected year | [2024](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_general_election,_2024 "Indian general election, 2024") |
**Ujjain** is one of the 29 [Lok Sabha](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lok_Sabha "Lok Sabha") constituencies in the [Indian state](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/States_and_union_territories_of_India "States and union territories of India") of [Madhya Pradesh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Madhya_Pradesh "Madhya Pradesh"). It covers the entire [Ujjain district](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ujjain_district "Ujjain district") and part of [Ratlam district](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ratlam_district "Ratlam district"). This constituency came into existence in 1951 as one of the [9th Lok Sabha](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/9th_Lok_Sabha "9th Lok Sabha") constituencies in the erstwhile [Madhya Bharat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Madhya_Bharat "Madhya Bharat") state. It has been reserved for candidates belonging to [scheduled castes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dalit "Dalit") since 1966.

# Ujjain Lok Sabha Election results 2024
Ujjain, a Lok Sabha constituency in Madhya Pradesh, was formed in 1951 and is one of 29 constituencies in the state. It includes Ujjain and part of Ratlam district. Reserved for scheduled caste candidates since 1966, the 2019 election saw Anil Firojiya of BJP emerge victorious with a significant margin of 3,65,637 votes over Babulal Malviya of INC. Firojiya secured 7,91,663 votes, retaining his position as the current MP. The constituency comprises Mahidpur, Ujjain Dakshin, Nagada-khachrod, Tarana (sc), Alot (sc), Badnagar, Ujjain Uttar, and Ghatiya (sc) assembly constituencies. Notable for a 75.33% voter turnout in 2019, 10 candidates contested. Ujjain Lok Sabha constituency remains a significant political area in Madhya Pradesh.

From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia
This is a [dynamic list](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:WikiProject_Lists#Dynamic_lists "Wikipedia:WikiProject Lists") and may never be able to satisfy particular standards for completeness. You can help by [editing the page](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Special:EditPage/List_of_people_from_Indore "Special:EditPage/List of people from Indore") to add missing items, with references to [reliable sources](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Reliable_sources "Wikipedia:Reliable sources").
The following list includes notable individuals who were born or have lived in [Indore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore "Indore"), [India](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/India "India"), or its surrounding towns and areas.

## Rulers, politicians and nationalists
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=List_of_people_from_Indore&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Rulers, politicians and nationalists")]

## Rulers, politicians and nationalists
*   [Rajesh Agarwal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rajesh_Agarwal "Rajesh Agarwal"), [deputy mayor of London for business](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deputy_Mayor_of_London_for_Business "Deputy Mayor of London for Business"), born in indore  
*   [Afroz Ahmad](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Afroz_Ahmad "Afroz Ahmad"), member in Indian government appointed by prime minister of India  
*   [Dr. Bhimrao Ambedkar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/B._R._Ambedkar "B. R. Ambedkar"), chairperson of Drafting Committee of Indian Constitution, social reformer, born in Mhow, District of Indore  
*   Field Marshal [K. M. Cariappa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/K._M._Cariappa "K. M. Cariappa"), first Indian [commander-in-chief](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Commander-in-Chief,_India "Commander-in-Chief, India") of the [Indian Army](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_Army "Indian Army"); studied at [Daly College](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daly_College "Daly College"), Indore  
*   [Homi F. Daji](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Homi_F._Daji "Homi F. Daji"), member of the 3rd Lok Sabha of India; represented the Indore constituency of Madhya Pradesh and was a member of the Communist Party of India  
*   [Ahilyabai Holkar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ahilyabai_Holkar "Ahilyabai Holkar"), ruler of [Holkar State](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Holkar_State "Holkar State"); built numerous temples, wells and dharamshalas all over India; spent most of her life in [Maheshwar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maheshwar "Maheshwar"), then capital of the Holkars; is said to have visited Indore only twice in her lifetime, but her name is synonymous with Indore and the university and airport are named after her  

## Rulers, politicians and nationalists
*   [Yashwant Rao Holkar II](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yashwant_Rao_Holkar_II "Yashwant Rao Holkar II") (born 1908), the [Maharaja of Indore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maharaja_of_Indore "Maharaja of Indore") belonging to the [Holkar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/House_of_Holkar "House of Holkar") dynasty of the Marathas; born in Indore  
*   Maharaja [Yashwantrao Holkar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yashwantrao_Holkar "Yashwantrao Holkar"), key figure in Maratha history; galvanized several years of resistance against the [British Empire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_Empire "British Empire"); called the 'Napoleon of India'  
*   [Ajit Jogi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ajit_Jogi "Ajit Jogi"), first [chief minister of Chhattisgarh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chief_Minister_of_Chhattisgarh "Chief Minister of Chhattisgarh"); district magistrate of Indore in the 1980s  
*   [Prabhash Joshi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prabhash_Joshi "Prabhash Joshi"), journalist, editor in chief of _[Jansatta](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jansatta "Jansatta")_ ([The Indian Express](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Indian_Express "The Indian Express") group)  
*   [Guru Radha Kishan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guru_Radha_Kishan "Guru Radha Kishan"), Swatantrata Sangram Sainik, fought for the economic deprivation for the poor and issues of social deprivation  

## Rulers, politicians and nationalists
*   [Sumitra Mahajan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sumitra_Mahajan "Sumitra Mahajan"), [Bharatiya Janata Party](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bharatiya_Janata_Party "Bharatiya Janata Party") (BJP) leader and MP; [member of Parliament](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Member_of_Parliament "Member of Parliament") from Indore Lok Sabha constituency since 1989 and lok sabha speaker  
*   Field Marshal [Sam Manekshaw](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sam_Manekshaw "Sam Manekshaw"), commandant of the Infantry School, [Mhow](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mhow "Mhow") during the 1950s  
*   [Ramesh Mendola](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ramesh_Mendola "Ramesh Mendola"), [Bharatiya Janata Party](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bharatiya_Janata_Party "Bharatiya Janata Party") (BJP) leader and MLA; [member of Legislative Assembly](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Member_of_Legislative_Assembly "Member of Legislative Assembly") from Indore-2 (Vidhan Sabha constituency) since 2008  
*   [Satyanarayan Patel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Satyanarayan_Patel "Satyanarayan Patel"), senior leader of Indian National Congress party  
*   [Jyotiraditya Scindia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jyotiraditya_Scindia "Jyotiraditya Scindia"), Indian politician, former president of [MPCA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Madhya_Pradesh_Cricket_Association "Madhya Pradesh Cricket Association"), hereditary patron of [Daly College](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daly_College "Daly College"), Indore  

## Rulers, politicians and nationalists
*   [Prakash Chandra Sethi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prakash_Chandra_Sethi "Prakash Chandra Sethi"), [Indian National Congress](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_National_Congress "Indian National Congress") politician; [chief minister of Madhya Pradesh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chief_Minister_of_Madhya_Pradesh "Chief Minister of Madhya Pradesh"); member of Parliament from Indore Lok Sabha constituency (1984–1989); served in a number of positions in the Centre, including home minister, defence minister, minister of external affairs, finance minister, railways, and housing and development  
*   [Digvijaya Singh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Digvijaya_Singh "Digvijaya Singh"), Indian politician; former [chief minister of Madhya Pradesh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chief_Minister_of_Madhya_Pradesh "Chief Minister of Madhya Pradesh"); senior leader of the Indian National Congress political party; studied at [Daly College](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daly_College "Daly College") in Indore; alumnus of [Shri Govindram Seksaria Institute of Technology and Science](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shri_Govindram_Seksaria_Institute_of_Technology_and_Science "Shri Govindram Seksaria Institute of Technology and Science"), Indore  
*   General [Krishnaswamy Sundarji](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Krishnaswamy_Sundarji "Krishnaswamy Sundarji"), commandant of the College of Combat, Mhow (now known as Army War College) during the early 1980s  
*   Air Chief Marshal [Shashindra Pal Tyagi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shashindra_Pal_Tyagi "Shashindra Pal Tyagi"), [chief of the Air Staff](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chief_of_Air_Staff_(India) "Chief of Air Staff (India)") of the [Indian Air Force](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_Air_Force "Indian Air Force"), 2004–2007  

## Rulers, politicians and nationalists
*   [Kailash Vijayvargiya](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kailash_Vijayvargiya "Kailash Vijayvargiya"), leader of Indore [BJP](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BJP "BJP"), currently serving as general secretary of the BJP

## Artists, writers and literary figures
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=List_of_people_from_Indore&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Artists, writers and literary figures")]
*   [Kunwar Amar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kunwar_Amar "Kunwar Amar"), hip-hop and contemporary style dancer; played lead role in _[Dil Dosti Dance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dil\_Dosti\_Dance "Dil Dosti Dance")_  
*   [Shubhangi Atre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shubhangi_Atre "Shubhangi Atre"), Indian television actor, had a lead role in _Bhabhiji Ghar par hai_, born and brought up in Indore  
*   [Digvijay Bhonsale](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Digvijay_Bhonsale "Digvijay Bhonsale") (born 1989), rock/metal musician, lead vocalist/guitarist of [Nicotine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nicotine_(band) "Nicotine (band)"), metal band from Indore; studied at [Daly College](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daly_College "Daly College"), Indore and [Cardiff Metropolitan University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardiff_Metropolitan_University "Cardiff Metropolitan University"), [UK](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UK "UK")  
*   [Meghdeep Bose](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Meghdeep_Bose "Meghdeep Bose"), Indian music composer, producer, arranger and singer  
*   [Puru Dadheech](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Puru_Dadheech "Puru Dadheech"), Padma Shri, Kathak scholar, dancer; holder of the first doctorate in Kathak classical dance in the world; attended high school in Indore and returned to settle since 1988  

## Artists, writers and literary figures
*   [Vijayendra Ghatge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vijayendra_Ghatge "Vijayendra Ghatge"), actor in the Hindi film industry; studied at [Daly College](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daly_College "Daly College"), son of Sita Raje Ghatge, who was the daughter of Maharaja [Tukojirao Holkar III](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tukojirao_Holkar_III "Tukojirao Holkar III") of Indore (reigned 1903–1926)  
*   [Hussain Haidry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hussain_Haidry "Hussain Haidry"), poet, writer and lyricist; born and brought up in Indore; studied at [Indian Institute of Management Indore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_Institute_of_Management_Indore "Indian Institute of Management Indore") and Government Arts and Commerce College, Indore  
*   [M. F. Husain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/M._F._Husain "M. F. Husain"), painter; spent his struggling years in Indore  
*   [Rahat Indori](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rahat_Indori "Rahat Indori"), Urdu poet and songwriter in Hindi films  
*   [Celina Jaitly](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celina_Jaitly "Celina Jaitly") (born 1981), Indian actress born in Shimla who mostly appears in Bollywood films  
*   [Ustaad Amir Khan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amir_Khan_(singer) "Amir Khan (singer)") (born 1912), celebrated Hindustani classical vocalist; referred to his unique style of khyal singing as "Indore Gharana"; born in Indore  
*   [Rais Khan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rais_Khan "Rais Khan") (born 1938), Indian sitar maestro; born in Indore  
*   [Salman Khan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Salman_Khan "Salman Khan") (born 1965), Indian film actor; Bollywood actor; born in Indore  

## Artists, writers and literary figures
*   [Shahbaz Khan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shahbaz_Khan_(actor) "Shahbaz Khan (actor)"), television actor, known for his role in _Chandrakanta_ as Kunwar Virendra Singh; son of Ustad [Amir Khan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amir_Khan_(singer) "Amir Khan (singer)"), born and raised in Indore  
*   [Sneha Khanwalkar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sneha_Khanwalkar "Sneha Khanwalkar"), Indian music director; works in Bollywood; was brought up in Indore  
*   [Swanand Kirkire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Swanand_Kirkire "Swanand Kirkire"), lyricist-singer-writer, born in Indore  
*   [Zakir Khan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zakir_Khan_(comedian) "Zakir Khan (comedian)"), stand-up comedian  
*   [Kiran Kumar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiran_Kumar "Kiran Kumar"), Mumbai-based Kashmiri Indian actor; studied at [Daly College](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daly_College "Daly College"), Indore  
*   [Kishore Kumar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kishore_Kumar "Kishore Kumar"), playback singer and actor; belonged to Khandwa; studied at the Indore Christian College and used to stay in the hostel  
*   [Lata Mangeshkar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lata_Mangeshkar "Lata Mangeshkar"), playback singer; born in Indore to Pandit Dinanath Mangeshkar  
*   [Mantra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mantra_(actor) "Mantra (actor)"), RJ, actor, comedian; born and raised in Indore  

## Artists, writers and literary figures
*   [Bhalu Mondhe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bhalchandra_Dattatray_Mondhe "Bhalchandra Dattatray Mondhe") (born 1944), [Padma Shri](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Padma_Shri "Padma Shri") awardee photographer, artist and environmentalist who played an important role in restoring the [Sirpur Lake](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sirpur_Lake "Sirpur Lake"), an important bird habitat and a [Ramsar site](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Ramsar_sites_in_India "List of Ramsar sites in India")  
*   [Praveen Morchhale](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Praveen_Morchhale "Praveen Morchhale"), filmmaker, educated in Indore  
*   [Palak Muchhal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palak_Muchhal "Palak Muchhal"), Indian playback singer; born and brought up in Indore  
*   [Palash Muchhal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palash_Muchhal "Palash Muchhal"), musical composer; born and brought up in Indore  
*   [Kumar Pallana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kumar_Pallana "Kumar Pallana") (1918–2013), Hollywood and Bollywood film actor, juggler, balance artist, teacher, yogi  
*   [Mahadevi Varma](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mahadevi_Varma "Mahadevi Varma"), Hindi poet; freedom fighter; was married to Dr Swarup Narain Varma in Indore  
*   [Johnny Walker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Johnny_Walker_(Indian_actor) "Johnny Walker (Indian actor)"), comedy actor; born in Indore

## Sportspersons and athletes
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=List_of_people_from_Indore&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Sportspersons and athletes")]

## Sportspersons and athletes
*   [Sandhya Agarwal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sandhya_Agarwal "Sandhya Agarwal"), former captain of [Indian women's cricket team](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_women's_cricket_team "Indian women's cricket team")  
*   Captain [Syed Mushtaq Ali](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Syed_Mushtaq_Ali "Syed Mushtaq Ali") (1914–2005), Indian international cricketer; Colonel Nayudu's teammate in the Holkar team and in the Indian team; popularly known as the 'Errol Flynn' of Indian cricket; born and died in Indore[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_people_from_Indore#cite_note-1)  
*   [Minoti Desai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Minoti_Desai "Minoti Desai") (born 1968), Indian cricketer, represented Indian women's team; born in Indore  
*   [Rahul Dravid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rahul_Dravid "Rahul Dravid"), Indian cricketer and former cricket captain; born in Indore  
*   [Raj Singh Dungarpur](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Raj_Singh_Dungarpur "Raj Singh Dungarpur"), former president of the [Board of Control for Cricket in India](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Board_of_Control_for_Cricket_in_India "Board of Control for Cricket in India"); former Indian cricket selector; ex-student of Daly College, Indore  
*   [Sydney Greve](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sydney_Greve "Sydney Greve") (1925–2015), prominent Anglo-Indian two-time Olympian representing Pakistan, played in the [1952 Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1952_Olympics "1952 Olympics") and the [1948 Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1948_Olympics "1948 Olympics")  
*   [Narendra Hirwani](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Narendra_Hirwani "Narendra Hirwani"), leg spin bowler and former member of Indian cricket team; moved to Indore as a teenager  

## Sportspersons and athletes
*   [Sanjay Jagdale](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sanjay_Jagdale "Sanjay Jagdale"), former state cricketer; presently a national selectors for the senior all-India teams and the honorary secretary of the Madhya Pradesh Cricket Association; director of the Cricket Club of Indore  
*   [Akshat Khamparia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Akshat_Khamparia "Akshat Khamparia") (born 1989), an Indian chess International Master; first player from Central India to hold an 'International Master' title  
*   [Venkatesh Iyer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Venkatesh_Iyer "Venkatesh Iyer"), cricketer, played for Indian team for some months, born in Indore  
*   [Avesh Khan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Avesh_Khan "Avesh Khan"), cricketer, born in Indore  
*   [Arundhati Kirkire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arundhati_Kirkire "Arundhati Kirkire"), born and brought up in Indore who played for the Indian women's cricket team  
*   [Shankar Lakshman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shankar_Lakshman "Shankar Lakshman") (1933–2006), goalkeeper of the Indian hockey team in the 1956, 1960 and 1964 Olympics and won two golds and a silver; captain of the team which won the gold in the 1966 Asian Games; belonged to Mhow and lived his retired life here until his death  
*   Colonel [C. K. Nayudu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C._K._Nayudu "C. K. Nayudu"), first Indian Test captain in cricket; led India between 1932 and 1934  
*   [Mir Ranjan Negi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mir_Ranjan_Negi "Mir Ranjan Negi"), hockey goalkeeper and coach of Indian women's team; won Asian Championship  
*   [Naman Ojha](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Naman_Ojha "Naman Ojha"), Indian wicket-keeper, stays and practices in Indore  

## Sportspersons and athletes
*   [Rajat Patidar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rajat_Patidar "Rajat Patidar"), cricketer, born in Indore  
*   [Chandu Sarwate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chandu_Sarwate "Chandu Sarwate"), former Indian cricketer and former Indian cricket selector; lived and died in Indore in 2003  
*   [Jalaj Saxena](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jalaj_Saxena "Jalaj Saxena") (born 1986), cricketer who plays as an all rounder for the India A cricket team; born in Indore

## Academia, business, research and professionals
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=List_of_people_from_Indore&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Academia, business, research and professionals")]
*   [Deepak Chaurasia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deepak_Chaurasia "Deepak Chaurasia"), journalist, editor in chief of _India News_  
*   [Seth Hukumchand](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seth_Hukumchand "Seth Hukumchand"), known as the 'cotton prince of India' and had much credit even in some overseas countries  
*   [Ravi Salgia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ravi_Salgia "Ravi Salgia"), translational thoracic oncologist, clinician/scientist, and academician  
*   Dr [S Prakash Tiwari](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/S_Prakash_Tiwari "S Prakash Tiwari"), former [vice-chancellor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vice-chancellor_(education) "Vice-chancellor (education)") of [S. K. Rajasthan Agricultural University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Swami_Keshwanand_Rajasthan_Agricultural_University "Swami Keshwanand Rajasthan Agricultural University"), [Bikaner](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bikaner "Bikaner"), and former director of [National Academy of Agricultural Research Management](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Academy_of_Agricultural_Research_Management "National Academy of Agricultural Research Management"), [Hyderabad](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hyderabad "Hyderabad")  
*   [Siddhartha Paul Tiwari](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Siddhartha_Paul_Tiwari "Siddhartha Paul Tiwari"), academician and researcher, UNESCO chair on technology and sustainability

**Vijayendra Ghatge** (born 1950) is an Indian actor in [Bollywood](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bollywood "Bollywood") film and television. He is known for the musical superhit movie _[Chitchor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chitchor "Chitchor")_ (1976). His other famous movies include _[Prem Rog](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prem\_Rog "Prem Rog")_ (1982), _[Devdas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Devdas\_(2002\_Hindi\_film) "Devdas (2002 Hindi film)")_ (2002) and _[Jhankaar Beats](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jhankaar\_Beats "Jhankaar Beats")_ (2003).

## Background and education
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Vijayendra_Ghatge&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Background and education")]
Ghatge is a member of the [Maratha](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maratha_Empire "Maratha Empire") royal family of [Kagal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kagal "Kagal") estate, which was a feudatory vassal of [Kolhapur State](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kolhapur_State "Kolhapur State"). He is thus a relative of the [Maharaja](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maharaja "Maharaja") of [Kolhapur](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kolhapur_State "Kolhapur State"), as [Chhatrapati Shahu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shahu_of_Kolhapur "Shahu of Kolhapur") was adopted from Kagal and placed on the Gadi of Kolhapur. Ghatge's mother, Sitaraje Ghatge, is the daughter of [Maharaja](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maharaja "Maharaja")[Tukoji Rao Holkar III](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tukojirao_Holkar_III "Tukojirao Holkar III") of [Indore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore_State "Indore State") (reigned 1903–1926) by his American-born third wife Nancy Miller (who was formally adopted by the Maharaja's aunt and took the name Sharmishtha Devi Holkar upon marrying the Maharaja).[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vijayendra_Ghatge#cite_note-1)[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vijayendra_Ghatge#cite_note-2) He is the paternal uncle of Indian actress [Sagarika Ghatge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sagarika_Ghatge "Sagarika Ghatge") (married to Indian cricketer [Zaheer Khan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zaheer_Khan "Zaheer Khan")), sometimes mistaken to be her father.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vijayendra_Ghatge#cite_note-3)

## Background and education
He is married to Avantika Ghatge who was formerly head of department of Fine Arts at the [Daly College](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daly_College "Daly College") in [Indore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore "Indore"). They have a daughter Umikaa Ghatge, who studied at the Daly College and is a freelance content writer.
After doing B.Com Honours (Management) from Sydenham College of Commerce, Bombay Vijayendra graduated in acting course from the [FTII, Pune](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FTII,_Pune "FTII, Pune").
Ghatge started his film career with a supporting role in [Rajshri Productions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rajshri_Productions "Rajshri Productions")' 1976 Hindi film _[Chitchor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chitchor "Chitchor")_. Directed by [Basu Chatterjee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Basu_Chatterjee "Basu Chatterjee"), the film was a box office "Superhit".[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vijayendra_Ghatge#cite_note-4) Thereafter, he did various supporting roles in films like _[Kasme Vaade](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kasme\_Vaade "Kasme Vaade")_ (1978), _[Tere Pyar Mein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tere\_Pyar\_Mein "Tere Pyar Mein")_, _[Prem Rog](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prem\_Rog "Prem Rog")_ (1982) and _[Razia Sultan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Razia\_Sultan\_(film) "Razia Sultan (film)")_ (1983). In the mid-1980s, Ghatge began appearing in television serials. His character role of Lala Vrishbhaan, played in the 1986–87 classic serial _[Buniyaad](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Buniyaad "Buniyaad")_ made him a household name.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vijayendra_Ghatge#cite_note-5)

## Background and education
In 2002, Ghatge appeared in the [Sanjay Leela Bhansali](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sanjay_Leela_Bhansali "Sanjay Leela Bhansali") directed _[Devdas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Devdas\_(2002\_Hindi\_film) "Devdas (2002 Hindi film)")_ in the role of Bhuvan Choudhary, the ageing husband of the heroine, Paro, played by [Aishwarya Rai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aishwarya_Rai "Aishwarya Rai").[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vijayendra_Ghatge#cite_note-6)

From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia
This is a [dynamic list](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:WikiProject_Lists#Dynamic_lists "Wikipedia:WikiProject Lists") and may never be able to satisfy particular standards for completeness. You can help by [editing the page](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Special:EditPage/List_of_people_from_Indore "Special:EditPage/List of people from Indore") to add missing items, with references to [reliable sources](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Reliable_sources "Wikipedia:Reliable sources").
The following list includes notable individuals who were born or have lived in [Indore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore "Indore"), [India](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/India "India"), or its surrounding towns and areas.

## Rulers, politicians and nationalists
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=List_of_people_from_Indore&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Rulers, politicians and nationalists")]
texts.2:
## Rulers, politicians and nationalists
*   [Rajesh Agarwal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rajesh_Agarwal "Rajesh Agarwal"), [deputy mayor of London for business](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deputy_Mayor_of_London_for_Business "Deputy Mayor of London for Business"), born in indore  
*   [Afroz Ahmad](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Afroz_Ahmad "Afroz Ahmad"), member in Indian government appointed by prime minister of India  
*   [Dr. Bhimrao Ambedkar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/B._R._Ambedkar "B. R. Ambedkar"), chairperson of Drafting Committee of Indian Constitution, social reformer, born in Mhow, District of Indore  
*   Field Marshal [K. M. Cariappa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/K._M._Cariappa "K. M. Cariappa"), first Indian [commander-in-chief](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Commander-in-Chief,_India "Commander-in-Chief, India") of the [Indian Army](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_Army "Indian Army"); studied at [Daly College](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daly_College "Daly College"), Indore  
*   [Homi F. Daji](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Homi_F._Daji "Homi F. Daji"), member of the 3rd Lok Sabha of India; represented the Indore constituency of Madhya Pradesh and was a member of the Communist Party of India  
*   [Ahilyabai Holkar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ahilyabai_Holkar "Ahilyabai Holkar"), ruler of [Holkar State](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Holkar_State "Holkar State"); built numerous temples, wells and dharamshalas all over India; spent most of her life in [Maheshwar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maheshwar "Maheshwar"), then capital of the Holkars; is said to have visited Indore only twice in her lifetime, but her name is synonymous with Indore and the university and airport are named after her
texts.3:
## Rulers, politicians and nationalists
*   [Yashwant Rao Holkar II](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yashwant_Rao_Holkar_II "Yashwant Rao Holkar II") (born 1908), the [Maharaja of Indore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maharaja_of_Indore "Maharaja of Indore") belonging to the [Holkar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/House_of_Holkar "House of Holkar") dynasty of the Marathas; born in Indore  
*   Maharaja [Yashwantrao Holkar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yashwantrao_Holkar "Yashwantrao Holkar"), key figure in Maratha history; galvanized several years of resistance against the [British Empire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_Empire "British Empire"); called the 'Napoleon of India'  
*   [Ajit Jogi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ajit_Jogi "Ajit Jogi"), first [chief minister of Chhattisgarh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chief_Minister_of_Chhattisgarh "Chief Minister of Chhattisgarh"); district magistrate of Indore in the 1980s  
*   [Prabhash Joshi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prabhash_Joshi "Prabhash Joshi"), journalist, editor in chief of _[Jansatta](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jansatta "Jansatta")_ ([The Indian Express](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Indian_Express "The Indian Express") group)  
*   [Guru Radha Kishan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guru_Radha_Kishan "Guru Radha Kishan"), Swatantrata Sangram Sainik, fought for the economic deprivation for the poor and issues of social deprivation
texts.4:
## Rulers, politicians and nationalists
*   [Sumitra Mahajan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sumitra_Mahajan "Sumitra Mahajan"), [Bharatiya Janata Party](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bharatiya_Janata_Party "Bharatiya Janata Party") (BJP) leader and MP; [member of Parliament](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Member_of_Parliament "Member of Parliament") from Indore Lok Sabha constituency since 1989 and lok sabha speaker  
*   Field Marshal [Sam Manekshaw](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sam_Manekshaw "Sam Manekshaw"), commandant of the Infantry School, [Mhow](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mhow "Mhow") during the 1950s  
*   [Ramesh Mendola](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ramesh_Mendola "Ramesh Mendola"), [Bharatiya Janata Party](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bharatiya_Janata_Party "Bharatiya Janata Party") (BJP) leader and MLA; [member of Legislative Assembly](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Member_of_Legislative_Assembly "Member of Legislative Assembly") from Indore-2 (Vidhan Sabha constituency) since 2008  
*   [Satyanarayan Patel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Satyanarayan_Patel "Satyanarayan Patel"), senior leader of Indian National Congress party  
*   [Jyotiraditya Scindia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jyotiraditya_Scindia "Jyotiraditya Scindia"), Indian politician, former president of [MPCA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Madhya_Pradesh_Cricket_Association "Madhya Pradesh Cricket Association"), hereditary patron of [Daly College](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daly_College "Daly College"), Indore

## Rulers, politicians and nationalists
*   [Prakash Chandra Sethi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prakash_Chandra_Sethi "Prakash Chandra Sethi"), [Indian National Congress](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_National_Congress "Indian National Congress") politician; [chief minister of Madhya Pradesh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chief_Minister_of_Madhya_Pradesh "Chief Minister of Madhya Pradesh"); member of Parliament from Indore Lok Sabha constituency (1984–1989); served in a number of positions in the Centre, including home minister, defence minister, minister of external affairs, finance minister, railways, and housing and development  
*   [Digvijaya Singh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Digvijaya_Singh "Digvijaya Singh"), Indian politician; former [chief minister of Madhya Pradesh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chief_Minister_of_Madhya_Pradesh "Chief Minister of Madhya Pradesh"); senior leader of the Indian National Congress political party; studied at [Daly College](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daly_College "Daly College") in Indore; alumnus of [Shri Govindram Seksaria Institute of Technology and Science](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shri_Govindram_Seksaria_Institute_of_Technology_and_Science "Shri Govindram Seksaria Institute of Technology and Science"), Indore  
*   General [Krishnaswamy Sundarji](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Krishnaswamy_Sundarji "Krishnaswamy Sundarji"), commandant of the College of Combat, Mhow (now known as Army War College) during the early 1980s  
*   Air Chief Marshal [Shashindra Pal Tyagi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shashindra_Pal_Tyagi "Shashindra Pal Tyagi"), [chief of the Air Staff](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chief_of_Air_Staff_(India) "Chief of Air Staff (India)") of the [Indian Air Force](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_Air_Force "Indian Air Force"), 2004–2007

## Artists, writers and literary figures
*   [Vijayendra Ghatge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vijayendra_Ghatge "Vijayendra Ghatge"), actor in the Hindi film industry; studied at [Daly College](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daly_College "Daly College"), son of Sita Raje Ghatge, who was the daughter of Maharaja [Tukojirao Holkar III](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tukojirao_Holkar_III "Tukojirao Holkar III") of Indore (reigned 1903–1926)

**Vijayendra Ghatge** (born 1950) is an Indian actor in [Bollywood](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bollywood "Bollywood") film and television. He is known for the musical superhit movie _[Chitchor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chitchor "Chitchor")_ (1976). His other famous movies include _[Prem Rog](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prem\_Rog "Prem Rog")_ (1982), _[Devdas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Devdas\_(2002\_Hindi\_film) "Devdas (2002 Hindi film)")_ (2002) and _[Jhankaar Beats](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jhankaar\_Beats "Jhankaar Beats")_ (2003).
texts.1:
## Background and education
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Vijayendra_Ghatge&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Background and education")]
Ghatge is a member of the [Maratha](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maratha_Empire "Maratha Empire") royal family of [Kagal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kagal "Kagal") estate, which was a feudatory vassal of [Kolhapur State](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kolhapur_State "Kolhapur State"). He is thus a relative of the [Maharaja](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maharaja "Maharaja") of [Kolhapur](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kolhapur_State "Kolhapur State"), as [Chhatrapati Shahu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shahu_of_Kolhapur "Shahu of Kolhapur") was adopted from Kagal and placed on the Gadi of Kolhapur. Ghatge's mother, Sitaraje Ghatge, is the daughter of [Maharaja](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maharaja "Maharaja")[Tukoji Rao Holkar III](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tukojirao_Holkar_III "Tukojirao Holkar III") of [Indore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore_State "Indore State") (reigned 1903–1926) by his American-born third wife Nancy Miller (who was formally adopted by the Maharaja's aunt and took the name Sharmishtha Devi Holkar upon marrying the Maharaja).[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vijayendra_Ghatge#cite_note-1)[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vijayendra_Ghatge#cite_note-2) He is the paternal uncle of Indian actress [Sagarika Ghatge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sagarika_Ghatge "Sagarika Ghatge") (married to Indian cricketer [Zaheer Khan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zaheer_Khan "Zaheer Khan")), sometimes mistaken to be her father.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vijayendra_Ghatge#cite_note-3)
texts.2:
## Background and education
He is married to Avantika Ghatge who was formerly head of department of Fine Arts at the [Daly College](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daly_College "Daly College") in [Indore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore "Indore"). They have a daughter Umikaa Ghatge, who studied at the Daly College and is a freelance content writer.
After doing B.Com Honours (Management) from Sydenham College of Commerce, Bombay Vijayendra graduated in acting course from the [FTII, Pune](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FTII,_Pune "FTII, Pune").
Ghatge started his film career with a supporting role in [Rajshri Productions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rajshri_Productions "Rajshri Productions")' 1976 Hindi film _[Chitchor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chitchor "Chitchor")_. Directed by [Basu Chatterjee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Basu_Chatterjee "Basu Chatterjee"), the film was a box office "Superhit".[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vijayendra_Ghatge#cite_note-4) Thereafter, he did various supporting roles in films like _[Kasme Vaade](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kasme\_Vaade "Kasme Vaade")_ (1978), _[Tere Pyar Mein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tere\_Pyar\_Mein "Tere Pyar Mein")_, _[Prem Rog](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prem\_Rog "Prem Rog")_ (1982) and _[Razia Sultan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Razia\_Sultan\_(film) "Razia Sultan (film)")_ (1983). In the mid-1980s, Ghatge began appearing in television serials. His character role of Lala Vrishbhaan, played in the 1986–87 classic serial _[Buniyaad](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Buniyaad "Buniyaad")_ made him a household name.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vijayendra_Ghatge#cite_note-5)
texts.3:
## Background and education
In 2002, Ghatge appeared in the [Sanjay Leela Bhansali](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sanjay_Leela_Bhansali "Sanjay Leela Bhansali") directed _[Devdas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Devdas\_(2002\_Hindi\_film) "Devdas (2002 Hindi film)")_ in the role of Bhuvan Choudhary, the ageing husband of the heroine, Paro, played by [Aishwarya Rai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aishwarya_Rai "Aishwarya Rai").[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vijayendra_Ghatge#cite_note-6)
