Modern-day Indore was established on the banks of the [Kanh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kanh_River "Kanh River") and [Saraswati](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saraswati_River_(Madhya_Pradesh) "Saraswati River (Madhya Pradesh)") rivers and traces its roots to its 16th-century founding as a trading hub between the [Deccan Plateau](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deccan_Plateau "Deccan Plateau") and [Delhi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Delhi "Delhi").[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-11)[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-12) Following the conquest of [Malwa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malwa "Malwa") by [Peshwa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peshwa "Peshwa")[Baji Rao I](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Baji_Rao_I "Baji Rao I"), the city came under the control of the [Maratha Empire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maratha_Confederacy "Maratha Confederacy") until its annexation by the [British East India Company](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_East_India_Company "British East India Company").[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-13)[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-14) Prior to [Indian independence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_independence_movement "Indian independence movement"), [the Kingdom of Indore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore_State "Indore State") was a nineteen [Gun Salute](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Salute_state "Salute state")[Princely State](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Princely_State "Princely State") of the [British Raj](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_Raj "British Raj") with the [Holkars](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/House_of_Holkar "House of Holkar") as rulers.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-15)

With an estimated population of 5.6 million in 2025 distributed over nearly 10 thousand square kilometres, the metropolitan region encompassing Indore, [Ujjain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ujjain "Ujjain"), [Dewas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dewas "Dewas"), [Pithampur](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pithampur "Pithampur") and [Nagda](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nagda "Nagda") serves as the financial capital of Madhya Pradesh. One of India's main industrial hubs, the metropolitan region is a major center for pharmaceutical and automotive manufacturing with, notably, [Asia’s longest test track](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NATRAX "NATRAX").[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-16)[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-17)[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-18)[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-19)[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-:6-20)

The largest education hub in central India, it is home to an [Indian Institute of Technology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_Institute_of_Technology_Indore "Indian Institute of Technology Indore") and an [Indian Institute of Management](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_Institute_of_Management_Indore "Indian Institute of Management Indore") and is one of the cities selected under the [central government's](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Government_of_India "Government of India") flagship [Smart Cities Mission](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smart_Cities_Mission "Smart Cities Mission") and [Swachh Survekshan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Swachh_Survekshan "Swachh Survekshan") programmes.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-21)[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-22)[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-23)[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-24)
Consistently ranked as India's [cleanest city](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_cleanest_cities_in_India "List of cleanest cities in India"), Indore is regularly commended for its clean air and proper waste management.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-25)[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-26)[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-27)[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-28)[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-29)[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-30)

## Etymology
[Gupta](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gupta_Empire "Gupta Empire") inscriptions name Indore as "Indrapura".[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-auto1-31) It is believed that the city is named after its Indreshwar Mahadev Temple, where [Shiva](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shiva "Shiva") is the presiding deity.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-32)[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-33) It is believed that [Indra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indra "Indra") himself did _[Tapasya](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tapas\_(Indian\_religions) "Tapas (Indian religions)")_ (meditation) in this place and led sage Swami Indrapuri to establish the temple. Later, [Tukoji Rao Holkar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tukoji_Rao_Holkar "Tukoji Rao Holkar") who belonged to the Holkar clan of the Marathas and was the feudatory of Indore, renovated the temple.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-34) The older name of Indore is believed to be **Indur**, as referenced in historical records.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-35) In 2017, a proposal was brought forward by the Indore Municipal Corporation to rename the city as "Indur".[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-36)[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-37)

## History
### Gupta Empire (Gupta era)
[Gupta Empire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gupta_Empire "Gupta Empire") inscription mentions Indore as city/town of Indrapura in Gupta Indore Copper plate inscription dated 146 Gupta era or 465 CE.[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-38) These are also some of the earliest mentions of Indore where the city is mentioned as 'Indrapura'.[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-39) Indrapura (modern day Indore) was then known for its sun temple, where in 464–65 CE, Gupta king [Skandagupta](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Skandagupta "Skandagupta") had made an endowment for the permanent maintenance of the city's sun temple. The temple was constructed by two merchants of the city – Achalavarman and Bhṛikuṇṭhasiṁha.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-auto1-31)[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-40)
[![Image 16](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/02/466_CE_Indore_Copper_Plate_Inscription%2C_Hinduism%2C_Skandagupta%2C_Sanskrit.jpg/250px-466_CE_Indore_Copper_Plate_Inscription%2C_Hinduism%2C_Skandagupta%2C_Sanskrit.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:466_CE_Indore_Copper_Plate_Inscription,_Hinduism,_Skandagupta,_Sanskrit.jpg)
An early Gupta era inscription from ancient India. This is a photograph of a personal copy of plates published by John Fleet in 1888, with Inscriptions of the Early Gupta Kings And Their Successors, as a part of the Corpus Inscriptionum Indicarum series, Vol. 3

## History
### Holkar era (Maratha Empire)
During the [Mughal era](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mughal_Empire "Mughal Empire"), the area under the modern Indore district was equally divided between the administrations (_[sarkar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sarkar\_(administrative\_division) "Sarkar (administrative division)")_ s) of [Ujjain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ujjain "Ujjain") and [Mandu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mandu,_Madhya_Pradesh "Mandu, Madhya Pradesh"). Kampel was the headquarters of a _mahal_ (administrative unit) under the Ujjain _sarkar_ of [Malwa Subah](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malwa_Subah "Malwa Subah") (province). The area of the modern Indore city was included in the [Kampel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kampel,_Indore "Kampel, Indore")[pargana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pargana "Pargana") (administrative unit).[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-gazetteer_1971-41)

## History
### Holkar era (Maratha Empire)
In 1715, the [Marathas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maratha_Empire "Maratha Empire") invaded this region (Mughal territory) and demanded [chauth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chauth "Chauth") (tax) from the Mughal _Amil_ (administrator) of Kampel. The Amil fled to [Ujjain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ujjain "Ujjain"), and the local [zamindars](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zamindar "Zamindar") agreed to pay Chauth to the Marathas. The chief zamindar, [Nandlal Chaudhary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rao_Nandlal_Chaudhary "Rao Nandlal Chaudhary") (later known as Nandlal Mandloi), paid a chauth of around Rs. 25,000 to the Marathas. [Jai Singh II](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jai_Singh_II "Jai Singh II"), the Mughal Governor of Malwa, reached Kampel on 8 May 1715, and defeated the Marathas in a battle near the village. The Marathas came back in early 1716, and raided Kampel in 1717. In March 1718, the Marathas, led by [Santaji Bhonsale](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bhonsle_(clan) "Bhonsle (clan)"), invaded Malwa again, but were unsuccessful this time.

## History
### Holkar era (Maratha Empire)
By 1720, the headquarters of the local pargana were transferred from Kampel to Indore, due to the increasing commercial activity in the city. In 1724, the Marathas under the new [Peshwa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peshwa "Peshwa")[Baji Rao I](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Baji_Rao_I "Baji Rao I"), launched a fresh attack on the Mughals in Malwa. Baji Rao I himself led the campaign, accompanied by his lieutenants [Udaji Rao Pawar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dhar_State "Dhar State"), [Malhar Rao Holkar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malhar_Rao_Holkar "Malhar Rao Holkar") and [Ranoji Scindia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ranoji_Scindia "Ranoji Scindia"). The Mughal [Nizam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Qamar-ud-din_Khan,_Asaf_Jah_I "Qamar-ud-din Khan, Asaf Jah I") met the [Peshwa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peshwa "Peshwa") at [Nalchha](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nalchha "Nalchha") on 18 May 1724, and acceded to his demand of collecting chauth from the area. The Peshwa returned to the [Deccan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deccan "Deccan"), but left [Malhar Rao Holkar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malhar_Rao_Holkar "Malhar Rao Holkar") at Indore to oversee the chauth collection.

## History
### Holkar era (Maratha Empire)
The Marathas maintained friendly relations with Nandlal Chaudhary, who held influence over the local [Sardars](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sardar "Sardar") (chiefs). In 1728, they defeated the Mughals decisively in the battle of [Amjhera](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battles_involving_the_Maratha_Empire "Battles involving the Maratha Empire"), and consolidated their authority in the area over the next few years. On 3 October 1730, [Malhar Rao Holkar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malhar_Rao_Holkar "Malhar Rao Holkar") was appointed as the Maratha chief of [Malwa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malwa "Malwa"). The local zamindars, who had the title of [Chaudhari](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chowdhury "Chowdhury"), came to be known as _Mandloi_ s (after [mandal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tehsil "Tehsil"), an administrative unit) during the [Maratha reign](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maratha_Empire "Maratha Empire"). The [Holkar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/House_of_Holkar "House of Holkar") dynasty of the Marathas, which controlled the region, conferred the title of _Rao_ upon the local zamindar family.[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-42) After Nandlal died, his son Tejkarana was accepted as the _Mandloi_ of Kampel by the [Peshwa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peshwa "Peshwa")[Baji Rao I](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Baji_Rao_I "Baji Rao I"). The pargana was formally granted to [Malhar Rao Holkar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malhar_Rao_Holkar "Malhar Rao Holkar") by merging 28 and one-half Pargana by the Peshwa in 1733. The pargana headquarters were transferred back to Kampel during his reign.

## History
### Holkar era (Maratha Empire)
After his death, his daughter-in-law [Ahilyabai Holkar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ahilyabai_Holkar "Ahilyabai Holkar") moved the headquarters to Indore in 1766. The [tehsil](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tehsil "Tehsil") of Kampel was converted into Indore tehsil by a change in the name.[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-gazetteer_1971-41) Ahilyabai Holkar moved the state's capital to [Maheshwar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maheshwar "Maheshwar") in 1767, but Indore remained an important commercial and military centre.

## History
### Princely State (Indore/Holkar State)
[![Image 17](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/25/Ahilya_Bai_Holkar_2025_stamp_of_India.jpg/250px-Ahilya_Bai_Holkar_2025_stamp_of_India.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Ahilya_Bai_Holkar_2025_stamp_of_India.jpg)
[Ahilyabai Holkar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ahilyabai_Holkar "Ahilyabai Holkar") on a 2025 stamp of India

## Demographics
### Languages
[Hindi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hindi "Hindi") is the official language of Indore city, it is spoken by over 80% of the population as their first language. A number of [Hindi dialects](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hindi_languages "Hindi languages") such as [Malvi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malvi_language "Malvi language"), [Nimadi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nimadi_language "Nimadi language") and [Bundeli](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bundeli_language "Bundeli language") are spoken in decent numbers by migrants from rural areas.
Of non-Hindi languages, the Marathi community has a sizeable presence (5%) from Maratha rule. Urdu is mostly spoken by the Muslim community. Sindhis, who are mostly traders, came as Partition refugees while the Gujaratis form a trading community. There is a small Punjabi Sikh community as well.[[66]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-Culture-66)[[67]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-Census2011-67)[[68]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-68)[[69]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-69)
According to 2012 figures, around 6,000 [Pakistani Hindu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hinduism_in_Pakistan "Hinduism in Pakistan") migrants live in the city (out of a total 10,000 in the state).[[70]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-70)

## Government and politics
### Civic administration
Indore has a city government, or municipality, with a mayor-council form of government. In 1870, the first municipality was constituted in Indore. Bakshi Khuman Singh (Commander In Chief) of Holkar State Army was appointed as chairman.[[71]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-:3-71) Indore municipality became the first city to have an elected municipal government responsible for the welfare and growth of the city.[[71]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-:3-71) In 1956, during the reorganisation of states, Indore was included in [Madhya Pradesh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Madhya_Pradesh "Madhya Pradesh"), and later that same year, was declared a [municipal corporation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Municipal_corporation "Municipal corporation").[[71]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-:3-71)

## Government and politics
### Civic administration
[Indore Municipal Corporation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore_Municipal_Corporation "Indore Municipal Corporation") (IMC) is spread over an area of 269 square km.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-villages-5)[[72]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-72) The Indore Municipal Corporation (IMC) is a unicameral body consisting of 69 Council members whose districts are divided into 12 zones and these zones had been further divided into 69 [wards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ward_(electoral_subdivision) "Ward (electoral subdivision)") defined by geographic population boundaries.[[73]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-73) In 2014, 29 villages were added into the fold of the municipality.[[74]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-74) In 2015, 23 more villages were added. After these inclusions, the number of wards went up to 85, and zones 19.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-villages-5)[[75]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-75)

## Government and politics
### Civic administration
The mayor and [councillors](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Councillor "Councillor") are elected to five-year terms. The municipal or local elections to Indore Municipal Corporation were last held in 2015.[[76]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-76)[[77]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-77) The next elections were to be held early in 2020, but as per a report from February 2020, these have not happened, although preparation of voter rolls and ward reservation happened later in July.[[78]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-78)[[79]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-79)[[80]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-80) The elected wing of the city government is headed by the Mayor and the incumbent Mayor is Pushya Mitra Bhargava. As per a report from the [Free Press Journal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Free_Press_Journal "The Free Press Journal"), Indore was notified in 2018 for not having constituted ward committees.[[81]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-81) The executive wing is headed by Pratibha Pal, the [municipal commissioner](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Municipal_Commissioner_(India) "Municipal Commissioner (India)") of Indore, who is also the first female commissioner of the city.[[82]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-82)
On 8 May 2020, the budget for of ₹ 4,763 crore for 2020–21 was approved for the civic body.[[83]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-83) Major sources of revenue for the municipality include collection of property tax, water tax, rent.[[84]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-84)[[85]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-85)

## Government and politics
### Civic administration
Indore municipality follows the guidelines as per the [Madhya Pradesh Municipal Corporations Act 1956](http://www.janaagraha.org/asics/report/Madhya-Pradesh-Municipal-Corporation-Act-1956.pdf)[Archived](https://web.archive.org/web/20180920174748/http://www.janaagraha.org/asics/report/Madhya-Pradesh-Municipal-Corporation-Act-1956.pdf) 20 September 2018 at the [Wayback Machine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wayback_Machine "Wayback Machine"), as well as the [Madhya Pradesh Municipalities Act, 1961](https://www.indiacode.nic.in/bitstream/123456789/3583/1/Municipal%20Corporation%20ACT%201961.pdf).[[86]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-86) The IMC is responsible for public education, correctional institutions, libraries, public safety, recreational facilities, sanitation, water supply, local planning, and welfare services.

## Government and politics
### Municipal finance
As per audited financial statements published on the CityFinance Portal,[[87]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-cityfinancehome-87) maintained by the [Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ministry_of_Housing_and_Urban_Affairs "Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs"), the Corporation reported total revenue receipts of ₹1,892 crore and total expenditure of ₹1,916 crore in 2022–23. The Corporation’s own-source revenue accounted for about half of its total receipts.
Composition of revenue receipts, Indore Municipal Corporation (FY 2022–23)[[88]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-cityfinanceindore-88)
1.   Own source revenue (50.1%)  
2.   Assigned revenue (34.7%)  
3.   Revenue grants (15.3%)
**Note:** Indore's total debt increased from ₹579 crore in 2021–22 to ₹760 crore in 2022–23, while its capital expenditure rose to 17.7% of total expenditure, reflecting improved investment spending.
_All figures are in crore rupees (₹ Cr)_

### Municipal finance

## Government and politics
### Representation in the parliament and state assembly
Indore city is represented in the parliament through the [Indore Lok Sabha constituency](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore_(Lok_Sabha_constituency) "Indore (Lok Sabha constituency)"), which covers most of the district.[[89]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-89) In May 2019, [Shankar Lalwani](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shankar_Lalwani "Shankar Lalwani") of [Bharatiya Janata Party](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bharatiya_Janata_Party "Bharatiya Janata Party"), who is also the chairman of the Indore Development Authority, had been elected as the [Member of Parliament](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Member_of_parliament,_Lok_Sabha "Member of parliament, Lok Sabha") from Indore.[[90]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-90)[[91]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-91) As per [delimitation from 2008](https://upload.indiacode.nic.in/showfile?actid=AC_CEN_3_20_00030_200233_1517807324510&type=order&filename=Delimitation%20Order,2008.pdf), Indore city is represented in the state assembly constituency through 5 Constituencies, election for which last took place in 2018:

## Government and politics
### Law and order
The [Indore Police](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore_Police "Indore Police"), a division of the [Madhya Pradesh Police](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Madhya_Pradesh_Police "Madhya Pradesh Police"), is under the direct control of Department of Home Affairs. The [government of Madhya Pradesh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Government_of_Madhya_Pradesh "Government of Madhya Pradesh") is the law enforcement agency in Indore. Indore district is divided into 39 police stations and seven police outposts.[[98]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-98)
In 2012, it was reported that the Police Commissionerate system would be implemented in Indore, but this did not pan out because of tussle between the IAS and IPS officers in the state.[[99]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-99) The bill was proposed again in 2018 and has been criticised by NewsClick.[[100]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-100) The system has not been implemented as of 2020, although there has been talk of it.[[101]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-101)
As of 4 September 2013, the Divisional commissioner is Dr Pawan Kumar Sharma.[[102]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-102) In Feb 2020, the new [Director General of Police](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Director_general_of_police "Director general of police") became Vivek Johri while SSP Indore is Harinarayan Chari Mishra.[[103]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-103)[[104]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-104)

# Indore
## Indore Overview
The city of Indore is known as the commercial hub of India as well as the leader in education for the entire country. Indore is also the most populated city in the Madhya Pradesh state of India. The city has been growing throughout its long history and, according to census figures, it shows no indication of slowing down.

# Indore
## City Size and Population Density
The city of Indore covers a sizeable area totaling 530 square kilometers (approximately 204.6 square miles). The overall population density in the metro area comes to 3,800 residents per square kilometer (about 9,700 residents per square mile).
The population of Indore is divided between those who live within the city and those residing in the surrounding areas. The population living in and around the city metro area totals 2,170,295 people, with 1,042,385 women and 1,127,385 men. The interior population is those that reside within the city limits, and this number equals 1,994,397 people, with 1,020,057 women and 944,029 men.

# Indore
## Religion
Religion is not of huge importance in many cities throughout the world these days - with religious affiliation rates falling consistently across the globe - but India is a significant exception to that growing trend.
Religion has always been an essential part of Indian life and [Indore remains primarily Hindu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#Demographics). Within the population of Indore, 80.18% of all people claim that they are of the Hindu religion. The second most practiced religion in the city is Islam at 14.09% of the population, followed by the Jain belief with 3.25% of the population. The remaining religions for the city of Indore are Sikhs at 1.09%, Christians at .65%, and Buddhists at .51% of the population. There is a small number (.21%) that claim no religious affiliation and the remaining .03% practice other religions.

# Indore
## Education
Education is a crucial focus for the population of Indore. The statistics show that Indore has one of the highest literacy rates in the world. With 85.87% of the total population being literate, the city has no choice but to be among the educational hubs in India. The literacy rates can be further broken down into males and female. The female population reflects a lower literacy rating than the male, with females at 81.48% and males at 89.9%. In terms of actual numbers, 885,014 men can read, while 739,648 of women are literate.

# Indore
## Unemployment
The unemployment rate of a city is quite remarkable. Although the focus on education tends to draw in new people to Indore each year with hopes for a better life, the unemployment rate might keep some away. The current unemployment rate for the city of Indore is 12.4%. That is quite high even for India, but the city has a history of the erratic unemployment rate. In contrast, the average unemployment rate for the whole of India is 5%. While there are many programs in place within the city, change takes time and progress can be slow.

texts.8: Modern-day Indore was established on the banks of the [Kanh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kanh_River "Kanh River") and [Saraswati](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saraswati_River_(Madhya_Pradesh) "Saraswati River (Madhya Pradesh)") rivers and traces its roots to its 16th-century founding as a trading hub between the [Deccan Plateau](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deccan_Plateau "Deccan Plateau") and [Delhi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Delhi "Delhi").[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-11)[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-12) Following the conquest of [Malwa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malwa "Malwa") by [Peshwa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peshwa "Peshwa")[Baji Rao I](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Baji_Rao_I "Baji Rao I"), the city came under the control of the [Maratha Empire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maratha_Confederacy "Maratha Confederacy") until its annexation by the [British East India Company](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_East_India_Company "British East India Company").[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-13)[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-14) Prior to [Indian independence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_independence_movement "Indian independence movement"), [the Kingdom of Indore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore_State "Indore State") was a nineteen [Gun Salute](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Salute_state "Salute state")[Princely State](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Princely_State "Princely State") of the [British Raj](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_Raj "British Raj") with the [Holkars](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/House_of_Holkar "House of Holkar") as rulers.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-15)

## Etymology
[Gupta](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gupta_Empire "Gupta Empire") inscriptions name Indore as "Indrapura".[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-auto1-31) It is believed that the city is named after its Indreshwar Mahadev Temple, where [Shiva](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shiva "Shiva") is the presiding deity.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-32)[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-33) It is believed that [Indra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indra "Indra") himself did _[Tapasya](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tapas\_(Indian\_religions) "Tapas (Indian religions)")_ (meditation) in this place and led sage Swami Indrapuri to establish the temple. Later, [Tukoji Rao Holkar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tukoji_Rao_Holkar "Tukoji Rao Holkar") who belonged to the Holkar clan of the Marathas and was the feudatory of Indore, renovated the temple.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-34) The older name of Indore is believed to be **Indur**, as referenced in historical records.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-35) In 2017, a proposal was brought forward by the Indore Municipal Corporation to rename the city as "Indur".[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-36)[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-37)

## History
### Gupta Empire (Gupta era)
[Gupta Empire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gupta_Empire "Gupta Empire") inscription mentions Indore as city/town of Indrapura in Gupta Indore Copper plate inscription dated 146 Gupta era or 465 CE.[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-38) These are also some of the earliest mentions of Indore where the city is mentioned as 'Indrapura'.[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-39) Indrapura (modern day Indore) was then known for its sun temple, where in 464–65 CE, Gupta king [Skandagupta](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Skandagupta "Skandagupta") had made an endowment for the permanent maintenance of the city's sun temple. The temple was constructed by two merchants of the city – Achalavarman and Bhṛikuṇṭhasiṁha.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-auto1-31)[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-40)

An early Gupta era inscription from ancient India. This is a photograph of a personal copy of plates published by John Fleet in 1888, with Inscriptions of the Early Gupta Kings And Their Successors, as a part of the Corpus Inscriptionum Indicarum series, Vol. 3

## History
### Holkar era (Maratha Empire)
During the [Mughal era](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mughal_Empire "Mughal Empire"), the area under the modern Indore district was equally divided between the administrations (_[sarkar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sarkar\_(administrative\_division) "Sarkar (administrative division)")_ s) of [Ujjain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ujjain "Ujjain") and [Mandu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mandu,_Madhya_Pradesh "Mandu, Madhya Pradesh"). Kampel was the headquarters of a _mahal_ (administrative unit) under the Ujjain _sarkar_ of [Malwa Subah](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malwa_Subah "Malwa Subah") (province). The area of the modern Indore city was included in the [Kampel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kampel,_Indore "Kampel, Indore")[pargana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pargana "Pargana") (administrative unit).[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-gazetteer_1971-41)
texts.14:
## History
### Holkar era (Maratha Empire)
In 1715, the [Marathas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maratha_Empire "Maratha Empire") invaded this region (Mughal territory) and demanded [chauth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chauth "Chauth") (tax) from the Mughal _Amil_ (administrator) of Kampel. The Amil fled to [Ujjain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ujjain "Ujjain"), and the local [zamindars](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zamindar "Zamindar") agreed to pay Chauth to the Marathas. The chief zamindar, [Nandlal Chaudhary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rao_Nandlal_Chaudhary "Rao Nandlal Chaudhary") (later known as Nandlal Mandloi), paid a chauth of around Rs. 25,000 to the Marathas. [Jai Singh II](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jai_Singh_II "Jai Singh II"), the Mughal Governor of Malwa, reached Kampel on 8 May 1715, and defeated the Marathas in a battle near the village. The Marathas came back in early 1716, and raided Kampel in 1717. In March 1718, the Marathas, led by [Santaji Bhonsale](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bhonsle_(clan) "Bhonsle (clan)"), invaded Malwa again, but were unsuccessful this time.
texts.15:
## History
### Holkar era (Maratha Empire)
By 1720, the headquarters of the local pargana were transferred from Kampel to Indore, due to the increasing commercial activity in the city. In 1724, the Marathas under the new [Peshwa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peshwa "Peshwa")[Baji Rao I](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Baji_Rao_I "Baji Rao I"), launched a fresh attack on the Mughals in Malwa. Baji Rao I himself led the campaign, accompanied by his lieutenants [Udaji Rao Pawar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dhar_State "Dhar State"), [Malhar Rao Holkar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malhar_Rao_Holkar "Malhar Rao Holkar") and [Ranoji Scindia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ranoji_Scindia "Ranoji Scindia"). The Mughal [Nizam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Qamar-ud-din_Khan,_Asaf_Jah_I "Qamar-ud-din Khan, Asaf Jah I") met the [Peshwa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peshwa "Peshwa") at [Nalchha](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nalchha "Nalchha") on 18 May 1724, and acceded to his demand of collecting chauth from the area. The Peshwa returned to the [Deccan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deccan "Deccan"), but left [Malhar Rao Holkar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malhar_Rao_Holkar "Malhar Rao Holkar") at Indore to oversee the chauth collection.

## History
### Holkar era (Maratha Empire)
The Marathas maintained friendly relations with Nandlal Chaudhary, who held influence over the local [Sardars](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sardar "Sardar") (chiefs). In 1728, they defeated the Mughals decisively in the battle of [Amjhera](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battles_involving_the_Maratha_Empire "Battles involving the Maratha Empire"), and consolidated their authority in the area over the next few years. On 3 October 1730, [Malhar Rao Holkar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malhar_Rao_Holkar "Malhar Rao Holkar") was appointed as the Maratha chief of [Malwa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malwa "Malwa"). The local zamindars, who had the title of [Chaudhari](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chowdhury "Chowdhury"), came to be known as _Mandloi_ s (after [mandal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tehsil "Tehsil"), an administrative unit) during the [Maratha reign](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maratha_Empire "Maratha Empire"). The [Holkar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/House_of_Holkar "House of Holkar") dynasty of the Marathas, which controlled the region, conferred the title of _Rao_ upon the local zamindar family.[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-42) After Nandlal died, his son Tejkarana was accepted as the _Mandloi_ of Kampel by the [Peshwa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peshwa "Peshwa")[Baji Rao I](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Baji_Rao_I "Baji Rao I"). The pargana was formally granted to [Malhar Rao Holkar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malhar_Rao_Holkar "Malhar Rao Holkar") by merging 28 and one-half Pargana by the Peshwa in 1733. The pargana headquarters were transferred back to Kampel during his reign.
texts.17:
## History
### Holkar era (Maratha Empire)
After his death, his daughter-in-law [Ahilyabai Holkar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ahilyabai_Holkar "Ahilyabai Holkar") moved the headquarters to Indore in 1766. The [tehsil](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tehsil "Tehsil") of Kampel was converted into Indore tehsil by a change in the name.[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-gazetteer_1971-41) Ahilyabai Holkar moved the state's capital to [Maheshwar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maheshwar "Maheshwar") in 1767, but Indore remained an important commercial and military centre.

## Demographics
### Languages
[Hindi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hindi "Hindi") is the official language of Indore city, it is spoken by over 80% of the population as their first language. A number of [Hindi dialects](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hindi_languages "Hindi languages") such as [Malvi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malvi_language "Malvi language"), [Nimadi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nimadi_language "Nimadi language") and [Bundeli](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bundeli_language "Bundeli language") are spoken in decent numbers by migrants from rural areas.
Of non-Hindi languages, the Marathi community has a sizeable presence (5%) from Maratha rule. Urdu is mostly spoken by the Muslim community. Sindhis, who are mostly traders, came as Partition refugees while the Gujaratis form a trading community. There is a small Punjabi Sikh community as well.[[66]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-Culture-66)[[67]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-Census2011-67)[[68]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-68)[[69]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-69)
According to 2012 figures, around 6,000 [Pakistani Hindu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hinduism_in_Pakistan "Hinduism in Pakistan") migrants live in the city (out of a total 10,000 in the state).[[70]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-70)
texts.38:
## Government and politics
### Civic administration
Indore has a city government, or municipality, with a mayor-council form of government. In 1870, the first municipality was constituted in Indore. Bakshi Khuman Singh (Commander In Chief) of Holkar State Army was appointed as chairman.[[71]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-:3-71) Indore municipality became the first city to have an elected municipal government responsible for the welfare and growth of the city.[[71]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-:3-71) In 1956, during the reorganisation of states, Indore was included in [Madhya Pradesh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Madhya_Pradesh "Madhya Pradesh"), and later that same year, was declared a [municipal corporation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Municipal_corporation "Municipal corporation").[[71]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-:3-71)
texts.39:
## Government and politics
### Civic administration
[Indore Municipal Corporation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore_Municipal_Corporation "Indore Municipal Corporation") (IMC) is spread over an area of 269 square km.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-villages-5)[[72]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-72) The Indore Municipal Corporation (IMC) is a unicameral body consisting of 69 Council members whose districts are divided into 12 zones and these zones had been further divided into 69 [wards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ward_(electoral_subdivision) "Ward (electoral subdivision)") defined by geographic population boundaries.[[73]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-73) In 2014, 29 villages were added into the fold of the municipality.[[74]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-74) In 2015, 23 more villages were added. After these inclusions, the number of wards went up to 85, and zones 19.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-villages-5)[[75]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-75)
texts.40:
## Government and politics
### Civic administration
The mayor and [councillors](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Councillor "Councillor") are elected to five-year terms. The municipal or local elections to Indore Municipal Corporation were last held in 2015.[[76]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-76)[[77]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-77) The next elections were to be held early in 2020, but as per a report from February 2020, these have not happened, although preparation of voter rolls and ward reservation happened later in July.[[78]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-78)[[79]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-79)[[80]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-80) The elected wing of the city government is headed by the Mayor and the incumbent Mayor is Pushya Mitra Bhargava. As per a report from the [Free Press Journal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Free_Press_Journal "The Free Press Journal"), Indore was notified in 2018 for not having constituted ward committees.[[81]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-81) The executive wing is headed by Pratibha Pal, the [municipal commissioner](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Municipal_Commissioner_(India) "Municipal Commissioner (India)") of Indore, who is also the first female commissioner of the city.[[82]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-82)
On 8 May 2020, the budget for of ₹ 4,763 crore for 2020–21 was approved for the civic body.[[83]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-83) Major sources of revenue for the municipality include collection of property tax, water tax, rent.[[84]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-84)[[85]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-85)

## Government and politics
### Civic administration
Indore municipality follows the guidelines as per the [Madhya Pradesh Municipal Corporations Act 1956](http://www.janaagraha.org/asics/report/Madhya-Pradesh-Municipal-Corporation-Act-1956.pdf)[Archived](https://web.archive.org/web/20180920174748/http://www.janaagraha.org/asics/report/Madhya-Pradesh-Municipal-Corporation-Act-1956.pdf) 20 September 2018 at the [Wayback Machine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wayback_Machine "Wayback Machine"), as well as the [Madhya Pradesh Municipalities Act, 1961](https://www.indiacode.nic.in/bitstream/123456789/3583/1/Municipal%20Corporation%20ACT%201961.pdf).[[86]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-86) The IMC is responsible for public education, correctional institutions, libraries, public safety, recreational facilities, sanitation, water supply, local planning, and welfare services.
texts.42:
## Government and politics
### Municipal finance
As per audited financial statements published on the CityFinance Portal,[[87]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-cityfinancehome-87) maintained by the [Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ministry_of_Housing_and_Urban_Affairs "Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs"), the Corporation reported total revenue receipts of ₹1,892 crore and total expenditure of ₹1,916 crore in 2022–23. The Corporation’s own-source revenue accounted for about half of its total receipts.
Composition of revenue receipts, Indore Municipal Corporation (FY 2022–23)[[88]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-cityfinanceindore-88)
1.   Own source revenue (50.1%)  
2.   Assigned revenue (34.7%)  
3.   Revenue grants (15.3%)
**Note:** Indore's total debt increased from ₹579 crore in 2021–22 to ₹760 crore in 2022–23, while its capital expenditure rose to 17.7% of total expenditure, reflecting improved investment spending.
_All figures are in crore rupees (₹ Cr)_

## Government and politics
### Representation in the parliament and state assembly
Indore city is represented in the parliament through the [Indore Lok Sabha constituency](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore_(Lok_Sabha_constituency) "Indore (Lok Sabha constituency)"), which covers most of the district.[[89]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-89) In May 2019, [Shankar Lalwani](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shankar_Lalwani "Shankar Lalwani") of [Bharatiya Janata Party](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bharatiya_Janata_Party "Bharatiya Janata Party"), who is also the chairman of the Indore Development Authority, had been elected as the [Member of Parliament](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Member_of_parliament,_Lok_Sabha "Member of parliament, Lok Sabha") from Indore.[[90]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-90)[[91]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-91) As per [delimitation from 2008](https://upload.indiacode.nic.in/showfile?actid=AC_CEN_3_20_00030_200233_1517807324510&type=order&filename=Delimitation%20Order,2008.pdf), Indore city is represented in the state assembly constituency through 5 Constituencies, election for which last took place in 2018:

## Government and politics
### Law and order
The [Indore Police](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore_Police "Indore Police"), a division of the [Madhya Pradesh Police](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Madhya_Pradesh_Police "Madhya Pradesh Police"), is under the direct control of Department of Home Affairs. The [government of Madhya Pradesh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Government_of_Madhya_Pradesh "Government of Madhya Pradesh") is the law enforcement agency in Indore. Indore district is divided into 39 police stations and seven police outposts.[[98]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-98)
In 2012, it was reported that the Police Commissionerate system would be implemented in Indore, but this did not pan out because of tussle between the IAS and IPS officers in the state.[[99]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-99) The bill was proposed again in 2018 and has been criticised by NewsClick.[[100]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-100) The system has not been implemented as of 2020, although there has been talk of it.[[101]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-101)
As of 4 September 2013, the Divisional commissioner is Dr Pawan Kumar Sharma.[[102]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-102) In Feb 2020, the new [Director General of Police](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Director_general_of_police "Director general of police") became Vivek Johri while SSP Indore is Harinarayan Chari Mishra.[[103]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-103)[[104]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-104)

# Indore
## Indore Overview
The city of Indore is known as the commercial hub of India as well as the leader in education for the entire country. Indore is also the most populated city in the Madhya Pradesh state of India. The city has been growing throughout its long history and, according to census figures, it shows no indication of slowing down.
texts.10:
# Indore
## City Size and Population Density
The city of Indore covers a sizeable area totaling 530 square kilometers (approximately 204.6 square miles). The overall population density in the metro area comes to 3,800 residents per square kilometer (about 9,700 residents per square mile).
The population of Indore is divided between those who live within the city and those residing in the surrounding areas. The population living in and around the city metro area totals 2,170,295 people, with 1,042,385 women and 1,127,385 men. The interior population is those that reside within the city limits, and this number equals 1,994,397 people, with 1,020,057 women and 944,029 men.
texts.11:
# Indore
## Religion
Religion is not of huge importance in many cities throughout the world these days - with religious affiliation rates falling consistently across the globe - but India is a significant exception to that growing trend.
Religion has always been an essential part of Indian life and [Indore remains primarily Hindu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#Demographics). Within the population of Indore, 80.18% of all people claim that they are of the Hindu religion. The second most practiced religion in the city is Islam at 14.09% of the population, followed by the Jain belief with 3.25% of the population. The remaining religions for the city of Indore are Sikhs at 1.09%, Christians at .65%, and Buddhists at .51% of the population. There is a small number (.21%) that claim no religious affiliation and the remaining .03% practice other religions.
texts.12:
# Indore
## Education
Education is a crucial focus for the population of Indore. The statistics show that Indore has one of the highest literacy rates in the world. With 85.87% of the total population being literate, the city has no choice but to be among the educational hubs in India. The literacy rates can be further broken down into males and female. The female population reflects a lower literacy rating than the male, with females at 81.48% and males at 89.9%. In terms of actual numbers, 885,014 men can read, while 739,648 of women are literate.
texts.13:
# Indore
## Unemployment
The unemployment rate of a city is quite remarkable. Although the focus on education tends to draw in new people to Indore each year with hopes for a better life, the unemployment rate might keep some away. The current unemployment rate for the city of Indore is 12.4%. That is quite high even for India, but the city has a history of the erratic unemployment rate. In contrast, the average unemployment rate for the whole of India is 5%. While there are many programs in place within the city, change takes time and progress can be slow.
